newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar holds support but spreads narrow.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar holds support but spreads narrow.

text.p: White sugar futures managed to hold above support at $300 basis March as the follow-through selling expected after the initial weakness on the spot position failed to materialise, traders said on Wednesday.
A handful of major players, including both trade and commission houses, continued to dominate activity in mostly piecemeal outright dealings, they said.
Some commission house crosses and light selling at the highs were also noted but traders said the afternoon session was nothing out of the ordinary.
With a firmer raws market, the spot premium remained broadly in line with Tuesday's close as New York consolidated after its recent sharp falls and funds held onto their long positions.

At 1652 GMT March was up $1.90 at $301.00 after opening at $299.00 and May was up $2.00 at $300.70. Nearby spreads narrowed as both May and August edged up to the $300 mark. March/May was reported to have traded at flat during the afternoon.
European sugar traders said they expected the results of Libya's buying tender by 1200 GMT on Thursday although the decision had been initially scheduled for Wednesday.
"They have postponed the decision until tomorrow," one trader said.

Turkey's state refiner Turkseker said it was still assessing bids for its tender to export 50,000 tonnes of whites, which could be concluded early on Thursday. A Turkseker official said it might consider splitting the offer into two or three parts.

Bidders are said to include local food and commodities traders Lebsan, Baykur, Naptat, Yilmazlar, Rotel, Ram and Fissan. E D & F Man and Andre have been named among the few international companies which participated.
Local traders said prices from some competing local companies ran as high as a $20 premium over Paris futures.
Paris trading was confined to the two nearby months, which were both $1.20 higher at $300.70. Matif volume was 1,054 lots.
The Paris exchange has announced two adjustments to the delivery process of its white sugar futures contract, to apply to the March and May 1998 expiries and onwards.
The seller of a contract may now deliver sugar either in polyjute or polypropylene bags. If polypropylene bags are chosen then the buyer is paid a packing differential.
The seller will be obliged specify either polyjute or polypropylene bags for delivery and to deliver a minimum net quantity of 2,500 tonnes.
